title: fleet-guards: CYCLE_MIN guard accepts leading-zero values (00 -> sleep 0 hot loop, 010 -> octal)
description: Codereview of n3y7 fix (correctness pass, kimi-k3). Case pattern ''|*[!0-9]*|0 rejects non-digits and literal 0 but passes 00, 08, 09, 010: '00' -> $((00*60))=0 -> sleep 0 -> unthrottled loop hammering bd + OpenRouter credits; '08'/'09' -> $((08*60)) fails 'value too great for base' -> sleep never runs (no set -e) -> same unthrottled loop; '010' -> octal 8 -> silently runs an 8-minute cycle. Fix: reject leading zeros in the pattern ('' | *[!0-9]* | 0*) — the load-bearing half; optionally force base 10 with $((10#CYCLE_MIN*60)) (base-10 alone does not fix 00).
close_reason: ALREADY FIXED on main — verified by execution, no code change needed. The bead's load-bearing ask (reject leading zeros) is present at main:scripts/fleet-guards.sh:11: case pattern ''|*[!0123456789]*|0* — executed against 0/00/08/09/010/000: ALL REJECTED; 5 and 1440 accepted. With leading zeros rejected at the case gate, $((CYCLE_MIN * 60)) (line 153) can never see octal form, so the bead's optional 10# hardening is moot. The 09 case (invalid octal) is covered by 0* too. Regression coverage: scripts/test_fleet_guards_cycle_min.py rejection matrix explicitly tests 0/00/08/010 in both default and globasciiranges-off bash environments — 2/2 pytest runs pass. Fix landed via 24bf422a84 + b57f1a8a1a (rejection matrix), pattern predates on main. No files touched this round (verification-only close); 3x codereview N/A — nothing changed to review.
